reviews.one: India decoupled from the global tech sell-off, riding historic FPI inflows and a ~17–19% plunge in crude prices to close Samvat 2082 and kick off Samvat 2083 above the Nifty 25,000 mark.
reviews.html:
What moved markets

  • Historic FPI Inflows: Foreign portfolio investors pumped over ₹45,970 crore ($4.11+ billion) into Indian equities over five sessions, driving the strongest weekly gain since February 2021 and overpowering past year-long sell-offs.
  • Crude Oil Tailwind: Brent crude suffered its biggest weekly drop since 2020 (~17% to 19% decline) as Middle East war premiums faded, providing a massive macro cushion for India's import bill and current account.
  • Robust Domestic Macro Fundamentals: India's growth narrative was reinforced by an IMF/RBI FY27 growth forecast upgrade to ~7%, alongside October GST collections surging 22.9% year-on-year to ₹2.31 lakh crore.
  • US Midterm Clarity vs. Global Yields: While a Democratic sweep in the US midterms eased trade and visa concerns, surging US Treasury yields and reviving Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations (72%-80% probability) stoked global volatility.
  • Q2 Earnings & Festive Resilience: Markets navigated mixed corporate earnings divergence alongside a late-week festive recovery, anchored by strong Dhanteras deliveries and record EV adoption despite initial headline auto retail dips.

Stories that developed during the week

  • Crude Oil & Oil-Linked Sectors: Initially reported midweek as a sharp ~19% decline driven by easing Middle East tensions, the crude narrative evolved by the weekend into managing extreme volatility and West Asian freight risks—prompting strategic shifts like IOC acquiring its own shipping fleet while continuously boosting OMCs and paint manufacturers.
  • Automobile Retail Demand vs. Wholesale Dispatches: The story began with FADA reporting a headline 23% drop in October retail auto sales due to festive calendar shifts and dealer inventory costs, but evolved positively as single-day Dhanteras deliveries, robust SUV demand, and a 93.6% surge in passenger EV registrations salvaged the November retail outlook.
  • Foreign Capital Rotation & Market Milestones: Starting the week marked by historic FPI selling across Samvat 2082, the narrative dramatically inverted as India emerged as a preferred hedge against global AI/tech sell-offs, resulting in record weekly inflows that pushed Nifty past 25,000 and set a high-water mark for domestic market capitalization ($5.31 trillion).

Sectors: who gained, who lost

  • Gained:
  • Banking & Financials: Outperformed on robust Q2 earnings, strong credit growth, and private bank strength (e.g., ICICI Bank, NBFC gold loans).
  • Oil & Gas: Benefited directly from plunging Brent crude prices lowering input and import costs for OMCs.
  • Metals & Mining: Bolstered by strong Q2 earnings beats and margin expansions from majors like Tata Steel.
  • Lost:
  • Cement, Capital Goods & FMCG: Grappled with severe margin compression due to rising raw material, power, freight, and input cost inflation (e.g., Thermax, Coromandel).
  • Telecom & Select IT: Weighed down by rising network expansion costs, shortening deal tenures, and corporate AI budget caps (e.g., Bharti Airtel Q3 misses).

Into next week

  • Monitor domestic retail inflation (CPI) data, which is projected to touch a 24-month high of 6.1%, threatening the RBI's threshold.
  • Track the sustainability of FPI inflows and post-Muhurat profit-booking trends following the sharp weekly market rally.
  • Watch the RBI's scheduled meeting with banks on November 12 regarding the implementation of the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework.
  • Keep an eye on upcoming corporate dividend record dates (CONCOR, HUDCO, NBCC, RITES) and prominent stock lock-in expiries between November 9–13.
